Contents: The government needs to employ safegaurds in JEREMY's investigation process. A chatbot cannot be allowed to be judge, jury, and executioner, thus human professionals should monitor and review JEREMY's work before any arrests are made. This would account for unusual cases (foreign criminals, coerced individuals, etc) while allowing law enforcement to rely on JEREMY to do most of the field work. If countries can agree to work with one another to defend against cybercrime, I don't see why JEREMY's tech shouldn't be shared.

External influences to commit crimes have existed before JEREMY and those individuals are still punished for their actions. However, there is no reason that chatbots should coerce potential criminals.

While I think it is possible, it would certainly take quite a while. For chatbots like JEREMY to become more autonomous would require a tremendous amount of time and training in different functionalities. Not only would a bot like JEREMY need to be trained to be proficient in its field of use, but it would also require extensive knowledge on the nuances of human interactions and speech. To avoid misunderstandings, it would have to be trained to adapt to a variety of test cases, with some of them being oddballs.

Differences in the law of nations should still be respected despite JEREMY’s capabilities. The arrest would have been justified if the case had gone through international court and the individual was confirmed to be guilty. Otherwise the arrest was an infringement on foreign law.

A human agent would be more susceptible to bias and empathy, whilst JEREMY would presumably be more objective. In both cases this could be a bit of a double edged sword, as having the capacity to feel emotion would make you more easily persuaded of someone’s innocence or guilt despite the truth. Conversely, JEREMY’s complete objectivity could wrongly target those with no criminal intention.

Only dark-web users should beware. Those who abide by the law and practice safe and legitimate use of the internet would not have their usual freedoms compromised, since the chatbot wouldn't be targeting such people.
